name: School Safety Checklist
description: A campus safety checklist covering drills, security, hazards and emergency plans.

items.text: Confirm written plans for fire, lockdown and evacuation.
Schedule and run required drills on time.
items.note: Vary conditions so responses become automatic.

items.text: Post evacuation maps and assembly points clearly.
Test fire alarms, smoke detectors and sprinklers.
Inspect extinguishers for charge and access.
Check first-aid kits and AED units are stocked and current.
Verify all exterior doors lock and latch properly.
Confirm no entry doors are propped open.
Test the intercom, buzzer or entry system.
Check that security cameras are working and recording.
Review who holds keys and access credentials.
Secure perimeter fencing and gates.
Walk hallways and stairs for trip and slip hazards.
Confirm exits and walkways are clear and unblocked.
Store cleaning chemicals locked and labeled.
Check playground equipment for damage and wear.
Inspect electrical outlets, cords and lighting.
Verify proper signage for wet floors and hazards.
Route visitors through one monitored entrance.
Require visitor sign-in and photo identification.
Issue and collect visible visitor badges.
Confirm staff supervision coverage at key times.
Verify authorized-pickup procedures are followed.
Keep a current record of who is on campus.
Confirm the mass notification system works.
Update emergency contact lists for staff and families.
Post emergency numbers in every classroom.
Confirm two-way radios are charged and working.
Review the plan for communicating with parents.
Brief all staff on their emergency roles.

faq.q: How often should we run safety drills?
faq.a: Fire, lockdown, and evacuation drills should run on a regular schedule throughout the year, often each term or as your local regulations require. Vary timing and conditions so staff and students practice responding even when the situation is unexpected.

faq.q: What are the most overlooked school safety issues?
faq.a: Common gaps include propped or unlocked exterior doors, expired or blocked fire extinguishers, outdated emergency contact lists, unsecured cleaning chemicals, and visitors who bypass sign-in. Regular walkthroughs against a checklist surface these before they cause harm.

faq.q: Who is responsible for school safety?
faq.a: Safety is a shared duty across administrators, teachers, support staff, and facilities teams, usually coordinated by a designated safety officer or committee. Assigning clear owners for each area keeps tasks from falling through the cracks.

faq.q: How do we manage visitors safely?
faq.a: Route all visitors through a single monitored entrance, require sign-in and identification, issue visible badges, and ensure staff know to challenge anyone without one. Keep a record of who is on campus in case of an emergency.

faq.q: Is this school safety checklist available as a printable PDF?
faq.a: Yes. You can print it or download it as a PDF for staff and administrators to use during walkthroughs, then tick off each item and assign follow-up for anything that needs attention.
